I'm working on /opt/nxeon-v2 (a Next.js design-fork of a hosting platform called Nxeon, branch design/v2). I just finished rebuilding the Billing page to closely match a design concept screenshot and real backend data. Now I need to move on to the "Activity" account page.

Please do the following research and report back (do NOT edit any files, this is read-only research):

1. Find the "Activity" page's current implementation: look for `app/dashboard/activity/page.tsx` (or similar) and its view component under `components/nx/` (likely `ActivityView.tsx`). Read them fully and summarize: what real data does it currently show, what's the current visual structure (hero, panels, lists, etc.)?

2. Find the design concept reference image(s) for the Activity page. Concept/reference images for this project live in board-upload directories under `/opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/<cardId>/`. Search these directories (there are several board cards) for an image that looks like an "Activity" page concept/mockup — it would show something like an activity feed/timeline/log UI for a hosting dashboard. Also check `/opt/nxeon-v2/design/concepts/` if it exists (there's supposedly an `activity.png` there per earlier project notes). List every candidate image path you find with a one-line description of what's in it (use the Read tool to actually view each candidate image, don't guess from filenames alone).

3. Check whether a hero illustration asset for the Activity page already exists at `/opt/nxeon-v2/public/nx/art/activity-hero.png` or `.webp` (there should be one from earlier work this session, extracted from a board upload).

4. Check what real backend data is available for an "activity" concept in this codebase — search for an activity log / audit log model in `prisma/schema.prisma` (grep for "Activity" or "AuditLog") and check `lib/nx/activity.ts` if it exists (it was referenced somewhere earlier). Summarize what real activity data (login events, deploys, payments, etc.) could genuinely be shown on this page without fabricating anything.

Report back with: the concept image path(s) and what they show, the current ActivityView.tsx structure/data, the hero asset path, and the real data model available for an activity feed. Keep the report focused and factual — under 400 words plus the image findings.

content.content:
design(v2): rebuild the six account pages on the concept screens

Referral, partner, settings, billing, activity, support and team were still the
production pages sitting inside the Nexion shell — which is why they read as
"very wide": they carry NO max-width at all and filled `<main>` (~1630px),
while the dashboard is capped at 1520. A shared `PageShell` now caps every one
of them, with a `narrow` variant (1180) for Settings, which is a single column
of forms where a long measure is harder to read. Measured after: 1304px of
content at a 1600 viewport, against the concept boards' ~1250.

Built from BOTH sources: the Claude Design artifact (63 artboards, extracted)
and the original PNG concepts on the board card, which are richer and which the
owner named as the target. Settings follows the PNG's left-rail layout rather
than the artboard's tabs.

REFERRAL AND AFFILIATE ARE ONE PAGE. /refer and /affiliate described the SAME
programme to the same customer in two vocabularies; /affiliate now redirects.
The partner half appears only for an account that actually is a partner.

Five models added, each because a concept screen needed something the schema
could not answer: ApiKey (hash only — the plaintext exists once, in the response
that creates it), UserSession, UserPreference, ReferralClick, OrgInvite. Plus
ReferralPartner.type and AuditLog.ip/orgId/target. All additive — a diff against
the live production database is 6 CreateTable, 1 AlterTable (two NULLABLE
columns), 5 AddForeignKey, 10 CreateIndex, and zero destructive statements.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, because the data does not exist and inventing
it would put a false statement in front of a customer:

  - The referral screen's "10% shared hosting / 5% VPS" cards. This platform
    pays a FLAT `referral_reward_cents` ($5) and percentages exist only on the
    partner side. The page is written around the real reward.
  - Support's "2m avg response" and "99.8% satisfaction". Nothing measures a
    first response and there is no satisfaction survey. An invented SLA is a
    promise the business never agreed to make.
  - Billing's "Nexion Pro $24.99/mo" plan card. There is no account-level
    subscription; Nxeon sells per service.
  - The concept's stack of three saved payment methods. This model holds ONE
    card and ONE vaulted PayPal.
  - Team roles Manager/Developer/Guest/Revoked, and "Create Role". The
    permission system enforces four roles; a badge for a role nothing checks
    advertises access that is not real.
  - Help Center and Service Status tabs — neither exists to link to.

TWO SECOND-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH TRAPS AVOIDED:

  - `UserPreference` originally carried notify* fields. Notification preferences
    already live in `User.notificationPrefs` behind lib/prefs.ts, which owns the
    policy about what may be suppressed — a declined payment or a 2FA change is
    delivered whatever the customer ticked. A second store the send path never
    reads is exactly the defect that file was written to fix. Removed; the page
    reads the existing prefs, and security alerts render as "Always on" rather
    than as a toggle that does nothing.
  - Activity categorises on READ, not write. `AuditLog.category` exists for new
    rows, but hundreds already have none and a backfill would make the same
    guess the code makes. The map was built from the real vocabulary grepped out
    of lib/ (36 server.*, 25 admin.*, 13 user.*, …); unknown prefixes fall to
    "Other" rather than being dropped, because a log that quietly omits things
    is the one thing a log may not be.

INVITES CAN NOW BE CANCELLED. They were stateless signed JWTs by design — see
lib/team-guard.ts on why the address is never resolved to a user id — but that

=== lib/nx/activity.ts ===
/* Turning an audit action into something a customer can read.
 *
 * `AuditLog.action` is a dotted machine string — "server.restart",
 * "wallet.topup", "user.login". The Activity screen groups by category, counts
 * per category, and prints a human title. All three come from HERE so the
 * counts and the labels cannot disagree.
 *
 * DERIVED, NOT STORED — on purpose. `AuditLog.category` exists for rows written
 * from now on, but the table already holds hundreds of rows with a null
 * category, and a backfill would have to make the same guess this function
 * makes. Reading through this means old rows categorise identically to new
 * ones, and changing the mapping does not require rewriting history.
 *
 * Unknown prefixes fall to "other" rather than being dropped: an action nobody
 * mapped is still something that happened to the account, and hiding it would
 * make the log quietly incomplete — the one thing a log may not be.
 */

export type Category = {
  key: string; label: string; icon: string; tone: string;
};

export const CATEGORIES: Category[] = [
  { key: "server",   label: "Servers & services", icon: "server",       tone: "#5fd0ff" },
  { key: "billing",  label: "Billing & payments", icon: "card",         tone: "#11c88e" },
  { key: "security", label: "Account & security", icon: "shieldcheck",  tone: "#f2b544" },
  { key: "network",  label: "Domains & network",  icon: "nodes",        tone: "#a855f7" },
  { key: "team",     label: "Team",               icon: "users2",       tone: "#7f9fe8" },
  { key: "files",    label: "Files & backups",    icon: "folder",       tone: "#5fd0ff" },
  { key: "database", label: "Databases",          icon: "database",     tone: "#f21cff" },
  { key: "other",    label: "Other",              icon: "activity",     tone: "#97b2e6" },
];

/** Action prefix → category. Prefixes come from the real vocabulary in lib/. */
const BY_PREFIX: Record<string, string> = {
  server: "server", gameserver: "server", hosting: "server", nxcloud: "server",
  volume: "server", node: "server", site: "server",
  wallet: "billing", invoice: "billing", payment: "billing", refund: "billing",
  coupon: "billing", partner: "billing",
  user: "security", auth: "security", admin: "security", session: "security",
  apikey: "security", sshkey: "security",
  domain: "network", dns: "network", ssl: "network", cloudflare: "network",
  mailbox: "network", company_mailbox: "network", discord: "network",
  org: "team", team: "team", member: "team",
  file: "files", backup: "files", snapshot: "files",
  db: "database", database: "database",
};

export function categoryOf(action: string): string {
  return BY_PREFIX[action.split(".")[0] ?? ""] ?? "other";
}

export function categoryMeta(key: string): Category {
  return CATEGORIES.find((c) => c.key === key) ?? CATEGORIES[CATEGORIES.length - 1];
}

/* Verbs that read the same to a person as they do in the string. Anything not
   here is de-dotted and sentence-cased, which is readable for the long tail
   without needing an entry per action. */
const VERBS: Record<string, string> = {
  login: "Signed in", logout: "Signed out",
  create: "Created", order: "Ordered", delete: "Deleted", destroy: "Deleted",
  start: "Started", stop: "Stopped", restart: "Restarted", reinstall: "Reinstalled",
  rename: "Renamed", resize: "Resized", snapshot: "Took a snapshot",
  restore: "Restored", topup: "Added funds", add: "Added", remove: "Removed",
  update: "Updated", renew: "Renewed", suspend: "Suspended", unsuspend: "Unsuspended",
  impersonate_start: "Started impersonating", impersonate_stop: "Stopped impersonating",
};

const NOUNS: Record<string, string> = {
  server: "server", gameserver: "game server", hosting: "hosting account",
  domain: "domain", wallet: "wallet", user: "account", ssl: "certificate",
  mailbox: "mailbox", volume: "volume", site: "site", org: "organisation",
  db: "database", backup: "backup", node: "node", partner: "partner",
};

/** "server.restart" → "Restarted server". Falls back to a readable de-dot. */
export function titleOf(action: string): string {
  const [head, ...rest] = action.split(".");
  const verb = VERBS[rest.join(".")];
  const noun = NOUNS[head];
  if (verb && noun) return `${verb} ${noun}`;
  if (verb) return verb;
  const words = action.replace(/[._]/g, " ").trim();
  return words.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + words.slice(1);
}

## 1. Current implementation

**`/opt/nxeon-v2/app/dashboard/activity/page.tsx`** — server component. Loads real data via `db.auditLog.findMany` (last `days` window — 7/30/90, default 30, up to 400 rows, newest first), a previous-period count for a delta comparison, and `db.userSession.count` for sign-ins. Categorizes each row on read via `categoryOf()` (stored `category` wins if present, else derived from the action prefix). Passes everything to `ActivityView`.

**`/opt/nxeon-v2/components/nx/ActivityView.tsx`** — client component, structure:
- `PageShell` hero: eyebrow "Activity", title "All your activity", subtitle stating the day window, tagline `["TRANSPARENT.", "SECURE.", "ALWAYS ON."]`.
- 4 `StatCard`s: Events (with ±% vs previous period, or "No earlier period" if nothing to compare), Server actions, Billing events, Sign-ins (shows "—" and "Not being recorded yet" if `UserSession` is empty).
- Two-column body: left = "Activity log" panel (search box, scrollable list of up to 120 events, each row shows icon, title via `titleOf(action)`, target/detail, IP, relative + absolute timestamp); right sidebar = "Period" (7/30/90d chips), "Categories" (checklist with per-category counts, toggle filter, reset), "About this log" (static blurb).
- Client-side filtering by category and free-text search over title/detail/target.

## 2. Concept image

Found the real concept mockup: **`/opt/nxeon/board-uploads/board/cmtmlv9k20p0nhl777grhs52y/25ddd9ee90589e4a72af7c98.png`** (1536×1024). This is a full Nexion-branded dashboard screenshot titled "ACTIVITY / All Your Activity." with subtitle "A complete log of your actions, events and account activity," a right-side aurora ribbon plus a handwritten-style "Every Action Matters" tagline and a glass "Transparent. Secure. Always On." card — matching `ActivityView.tsx`'s tagline array exactly. Below the hero: 4 stat tiles (142 Total Actions +12%, 8 Login Sessions +33%, 28 Server Actions +7%, 14 Payments +40%), a wide "Activity Logs" table (Time/User/Action/Details/IP Address columns, e.g. "Server Restarted", "Payment Made", "Team Member Invited", "Successful Login"), and a right rail "Filter Activity" panel with date range + a category checklist (All Categories, Server Actions, Billing & Payments, Account & Security, Team Management, File Management, Database Actions, Schedules, Other) plus counts — this is clearly the direct source for `CATEGORIES` in `lib/nx/activity.ts`.

The same board directory (`cmtmlv9k20p0nhl777grhs52y`, 25 images, all 1536×1024) contains sibling concepts for the other account pages already built: `0509e98a9b2370debda7d449.png` = Team, `0aa94bfb3094415a900f386a.png` = main Dashboard, `2d7ee52e4984c7bd773b787b.png` = Matrix, `30adfc6df1d8dbc88e51809f.png` = a game-server (Palworld) detail page. This confirms it's the single "board card" the `6aef354` commit refers to ("the original PNG concepts on the board card").

No `design/concepts/` directory exists in `/opt/nxeon-v2` (checked — not present), so that earlier-noted path is stale/incorrect.

## 3. Hero asset

`/opt/nxeon-v2/public/nx/art/activity-hero.png` (1400×901) and `activity-hero.webp` both exist, dated today 07:44 — generated alongside billing/partner/settings/support heroes in the same batch. It is not a pixel-identical crop of the concept PNG (different resolution, 1536×1024 vs 1400×901) but is very plausibly an AI re-render/extraction of the aurora-ribbon element from that same concept image (same ~0.64 height/width ratio pattern shared by all five sibling heroes).

## 4. Real backend data available

- **`AuditLog`** (`prisma/schema.prisma` ~line 934): `id, userId, action, detail, createdAt, ip, category, orgId, target`. `category` is nullable/derived-on-read via `lib/nx/activity.ts`'s `categoryOf()`, mapping action prefixes (`server/gameserver/hosting/nxcloud/volume/node/site`→server, `wallet/invoice/payment/refund/coupon/partner`→billing, `user/auth/admin/session/apikey/sshkey`→security, `domain/dns/ssl/cloudflare/mailbox/discord`→network, `org/team/member`→team, `file/backup/snapshot`→files, `db/database`→database, else "other"). `titleOf()` turns e.g. `server.restart` into "Restarted server".
- **`UserSession`** (~line 5542): `id, userId, tokenHash, userAgent, ip, location, lastSeenAt, revokedAt, createdAt` — used for the Sign-ins stat; currently new/empty until sign-ins start being recorded (page already handles this honestly as "—"/"Not being recorded yet" rather than showing 0).

This genuinely supports: server/service actions (restarts, deploys, backups, database creation), billing/payment events, security events (logins, API key/SSH key changes), domain/DNS changes, team/org membership changes, and file/backup actions — all real, queryable, already wired into the existing page/view. Nothing like "avg response time" or invented SLA metrics is backed by any model, consistent with the prior commit's stated policy of not fabricating data.
